name: Deadlock
principle: Two or more threads or executable segments acquire and hold locks in a cycle, so each waits for another to release a needed lock. The result is permanent blocking of progress and loss of availability.
detection_signals: Nested acquisition of multiple mutexes/monitors in different orders across functions
`pthread_mutex_lock()` / `std::mutex::lock()` / `synchronized` blocks where unlock is not guaranteed on every exit path
Holding one lock while calling into another function that may acquire a second lock or invoke callbacks
`wait()`/`join()`/blocking I/O performed while a lock is held
Two threads share locks `A` and `B` and code paths lock `A->B` in one place and `B->A` in another
Busy-wait or retry loop on `try_lock()` without releasing already-held locks
negative_signals: Only one shared lock is ever used
All code paths enforce a single global lock order for every pair of locks
`tryLock()`/timed lock failure always releases held locks before retrying
RAII/`finally`/`defer` ensures every lock has a paired unlock on exceptions and returns
No blocking calls or external callbacks occur while a lock is held
false_defense_traps: Using `tryLock()` but spinning while still holding another lock
Relying on `sleep()` or a timeout to break a circular wait
Wrapping lock release in code that is skipped by exceptions, `return`, or `goto`
Using `synchronized`/`monitor` blocks but calling unknown code inside the block
verification_focus: Can any execution path hold one lock while waiting for another, creating a circular wait with no guaranteed release or timeout?

consequence_chains.trigger: concurrent interleaving changes lock acquisition or release order
consequence_chains.consequence: threads block forever and service availability is lost

patch_principle: Define and enforce one global lock acquisition order
Minimize lock scope; release before blocking calls or callbacks
Use `try_lock`/timed acquisition with rollback on failure
Ensure every exit path releases all held locks, including exceptions

minimal_examples.vuln: T1: lock(A); lock(B); work(); unlock(B); unlock(A);   T2: lock(B); lock(A); work(); unlock(A); unlock(B);
minimal_examples.safe: T1: lock(A); lock(B); work(); unlock(B); unlock(A);   T2: lock(A); lock(B); work(); unlock(B); unlock(A);
